faqs.q: How many cups of coffee a day are safe?
faqs.a: For most healthy adults, up to about 400 mg of caffeine a day is considered safe, which is roughly three to four regular cups of brewed coffee. The caffeine in a cup varies a lot with its size, strength and type, and tea, cola and energy drinks also add to your total, so cut back if you feel jittery or sleep badly.

faqs.q: Is it bad to drink coffee on an empty stomach?
faqs.a: For most people it is not harmful, but coffee on an empty stomach can trigger acidity, heartburn or an upset stomach in those who are sensitive. If that happens to you, have it with or after some food. Frequent or severe acidity is worth discussing with a doctor.

Moderate coffee drinking does not usually dehydrate you. Caffeine has a mild diuretic effect, but the water in the coffee largely makes up for it, so it still counts towards your daily fluids. It is still best to drink water through the day rather than relying on coffee alone.

faqs.q: Can I drink coffee during pregnancy?
faqs.a: Pregnant women are generally advised to limit caffeine rather than give it up entirely, with major health bodies suggesting staying under about 200 mg a day, roughly one to two small cups of coffee. Because caffeine also comes from tea, chocolate and soft drinks, and needs vary, check with your doctor about what is right for you.
